headline: Stocks steady into CPI as oil retreats from four-year highs
body: Equities notched a fourth straight down session Thursday, with the S&P 500 off 0.58% to 7,591.70, the Nasdaq down 0.65% to 26,081.72, and the Dow shedding 0.6% to 52,064.10. The VIX closed above 17 for the first time in 28 sessions, a meaningful shift from the complacency that had prevailed through the summer, though still short of stress territory. The proximate driver has been energy and rates: Brent crude topped $107 and WTI touched $100 this week as Gulf tensions escalated, while the 10-year Treasury yield pushed to its highest level since 2023. A hotter-than-expected PPI print added to the unease, with headline producer prices up 5.4% year-over-year and core at a multi-month high, muddying the inflation picture just days before the Fed's September 15-16 meeting.

Futures are calmer heading into Friday, with the S&P, Nasdaq, and Dow all pointing modestly higher, helped by oil giving back some of its spike overnight. The session's real focus is the August CPI report at 8:30am ET — the last inflation read before the Fed enters its pre-meeting blackout — with headline inflation expected around 3.4% year-over-year and core near 2.4%. Given this week's hot PPI, the market's reaction function looks unusually sensitive to any upside surprise. Retail chatter was thin in today's scan, with no concrete social-sentiment wave to point to, so this read leans on price action and the data calendar rather than positioning signals.
